Decision — screenshot

Status: accepted 2026-10-12; amended 2026-10-13 (saved shots are named YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.png, as Spectacle can name them, instead of Screenshot YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM-SS.png). Amends the source layout (AGENTS.md §3.4).

The decision

  • The screenshot and annotation app is apps/screenshot. Its package, binary and directory are screenshot, its app id is dev.mixos.screenshot and its Bus service and verbs are screenshot and screenshot.*. "Screenshot" is exactly what the app does, and it is the word a person looks for in a launcher.

  • It supersedes Cap. Cap was the iced screenshot app (apps/cap, dev.mixos.cap, verbs cap.*) that lived outside this tree. The egui port brings its behaviour across under the new name:

    • the engine moves into the annotation crate: the immutable capture, the editable objects with undo, one painter for preview and export, and no-clobber PNG publication;
    • the iced shell is rewritten on the toolkit, with every action a registry command.

    Cap's names are retired and stay reserved (§3.5): the binary cap, the app id dev.mixos.cap and the verbs cap.ping, cap.info, cap.capture, cap.cancel, cap.open, cap.annotate, cap.move, cap.delete, cap.crop, cap.undo, cap.redo, cap.export, cap.show and cap.quit. They are entered in the retired-names registry when it lands. None of them was ever registered here.

  • Print Screen starts it. compd's bindings, in both profiles:

    • Print takes a region;
    • Shift+Print takes the whole output;
    • Alt+Print takes the window that had the keyboard.

    compd launches screenshot --comp SERVICE --capture MODE, naming its own Bus service (so a nested compd's key captures through that compd) and, for a window capture, the window that had the keyboard at the key press. There is one window and one headless instance per compositor: screenshot and screenshot-headless for comp, screenshot-<comp> and screenshot-headless-<comp> for another when the name fits in 31 bytes, else screenshot--<hash> and screenshot-headless--<hash>; a window name never starts with screenshot-headless. If that window is already running, the new process hands the request to it over the Bus (screenshot.take) and exits. Unsaved annotations are never discarded by a key press: the window comes forward and asks first.

  • Saved shots go to the screenshots folder. Save (Ctrl+S) writes XDG_PICTURES_DIR/Screenshots/YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.png (local time) with no dialog. A taken name gets _2, _3 and so on, and nothing is ever replaced. Every save is published on screenshot.saved and recorded, so an agent gets the latest shots from screenshot.recent without being told a path.

  • screenshot is an accepted name collision.

    • Arch Linux's extra/nwg-shell installs /usr/bin/screenshot, a helper for that shell. It was the only owner found on 2026-10-12, checked with pacman -F.
    • In Debian trixie no package installs a screenshot in a binary directory. The name appears only inside private directories (a GIMP plug-in, the Qt examples), checked with the packages.debian.org contents search.
    • Fedora was not checked: it has no public file search that works without a Fedora host.
    • MixOS installs to /opt/mixos/bin, which comes first in its PATH, so a MixOS session's screenshot is this one. compd launches it from its own directory, and the desktop entry names it by absolute path.

Why

The plain word is the right name for the plain job, and cap said nothing to someone who did not already know it. The collision costs little: nwg-shell's helper is internal to nwg-shell and is not run by name inside a MixOS session.

Handing a shot to an agent should need no typing. A fixed folder, a name that sorts by time, a topic on every save and a query for the latest shots give the agent the file without the person saying where it is.

Consequences

  • AGENTS.md §3.4 lists the accepted collisions: mix (Elixir), rec and play (sox), and screenshot (nwg-shell).
  • The screenshot.* verbs and its drive verbs are registered in docs/docs/spec/bus/verbs.conf.mix.
  • compd's binding table gains Print, Shift+Print and Alt+Print. No bare F1–F12 key is bound: those belong to the person.
